The resulting theory of sensitivity is based on the Wasserstein geometry in the same way that the classical theory of variance is based on the Fisher-Rao (equivalently, Hellinger) geometry, and this insight allows us to determine a collection of results which are analogous to the classical case: a Wasserstein-Cram\'er-Rao lower bound for the sensitivity of any unbiased estimator, a characterization of models in which there exist unbiased estimators achieving the lower bound exactly, and various results on the asymptotic achievement of the lower bound. More precisely, we show that Wasserstein projection estimators (and one-step approximations thereof) are asymptotically sensitivity-efficient under suitable assumptions, and that there exist Hodges-type estimators which exhibit super-sensitivity-efficiency. We use these results to treat many statistical examples, sometimes revealing new optimality properties for existing estimators and other times revealing entirely new estimators.
item.dc:creator: Nicol\'as Garc\'ia Trillos, Adam Quinn Jaffe, Bodhisattva Sen

item.title: Certified bounds on optimization problems in quantum theory
item.description: arXiv:2512.17713v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Semidefinite relaxations of polynomial optimization have become a central tool for addressing the non-convex optimization problems over non-commutative operators that are ubiquitous in quantum information theory and, more in general, quantum physics. Yet, as these global relaxation methods are solved numerically, the bounds issued by the semidefinite solver can - and often do - exceed the global optimum, undermining their certifiability. To counter this issue, we introduce a framework for extracting rigorous certified bounds on non-commutative optimization problems from inexact numerical data, and apply it to several paradigmatic problems in quantum information theory. An extension to sparsity and symmetry-adapted semidefinite relaxations is also provided and compared to the general dense scheme. Our results establish rational post-processing as a practical route to reliable certification, pushing semidefinite optimization toward a certifiable standard for quantum information science.
item.dc:creator: Younes Naceur, Jie Wang, Victor Magron, Antonio Ac\'in

item.title: Decentralized Multi-product Pricing: Diagonal Dominance, Nash Equilibrium, and Price of Anarchy
item.description: arXiv:2601.18117v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Decentralized pricing in multi-product firms and marketplaces can lose revenue because each decision maker ignores how its price affects the demand for other products. We quantify this loss through the price of anarchy of a game in which the price of each product is set to maximize that product's own revenue. Demand is linear, and cross-price effects may be substitutes or complements and need not be symmetric. Under a two-sided diagonal dominance condition with parameter $\mu\in[0,1)$, which bounds the aggregate absolute cross-price effects in each row and column relative to the own-price effect, we show that the game has a unique Nash equilibrium and that equilibrium revenue is at least a fraction $4(1-\mu)/(2-\mu)^2$ of the centralized optimum. This bound was previously known for symmetric gross substitutes; we show that it remains valid for signed and asymmetric interactions, and that it is tight. Because asymmetry breaks the simultaneous diagonalization underlying existing analyses, we instead evaluate the revenue gap at the equilibrium itself. This yields an exact formula for the worst-case price of anarchy of each demand matrix in terms of a normalized interaction matrix, which can be much sharper than the scalar bound in heterogeneous interaction networks. The same argument extends the guarantee to jointly concave nonlinear demand under pointwise dominance of the demand Jacobian, for every pure-strategy equilibrium.
item.dc:creator: Boxiao Chen, Jiashuo Jiang, Stefanus Jasin

item.title: Neuromorphic Realization of Best Response in Finite-Action Games
item.description: arXiv:2604.03222v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a mechanistic dynamical-systems formulation of best response in finite-action games with relational structure on the action set. The proposed neuromorphic decision dynamics realize best response as the stable outcome of an internal state-space process, rather than as an externally imposed choice rule. This provides a deterministic account of commitment formation, symmetry resolution through basins of attraction, and hysteresis and decision persistence under perturbations. For action spaces with circulant coupling, we prove using Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction that the action-coupling operator determines which components of evidence govern decision formation. We further show that the dynamics implicitly compute a geometry-aware utility, converge exponentially to the corresponding best response, and switch only when evidence is sufficiently strong. In contrast, supplying the same geometry-aware utility directly to logit dynamics does not recover these properties, showing that relational structure must be embedded in the decision mechanism itself. We illustrate the framework in a repeated coverage game, prove that the induced game is an exact potential game, and show that its Nash equilibria are reached by the neuromorphic decision dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Himani Sinhmar, Vaibhav Srivastava, Naomi Ehrich Leonard

item.title: Distributed Optimization with Nesterov Momentum and Finite-Time Quantized Averaging over Directed Networks: Extended Version
item.description: arXiv:2604.16906v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In modern large-scale networked systems, rapidly solving optimization problems while utilizing communication resources efficiently is critical for addressing complex tasks. However, distributed optimization over bandwidth-limited networks must cope with two obstacles: limited-bandwidth communication, and slow convergence when the objective is ill-conditioned. In this paper, we consider unconstrained distributed optimization over strongly connected directed networks, where nodes exchange quantized (i.e., compressed) messages. We propose QANM (Quantized Averaged Nesterov Momentum), an algorithm that combines Nesterov momentum with a finite-time quantized averaging protocol. At every iteration, QANM enables all nodes to reach exact agreement, without requiring doubly stochastic weight matrices or undirected communication. For strongly convex and smooth objectives, we show that the objective gap of QANM decays at the accelerated rate $1-\kappa^{-1/2}$ (where $\kappa$ is the condition number), up to a residual of order $\Delta^2$ determined by the quantization level $\Delta$. This improves the condition-number dependence of the transient iteration complexity from $\kappa$ to $\sqrt{\kappa}$ compared with gradient descent that utilizes the same quantized averaging mechanism. Finally, we evaluate QANM on a distributed sensor fusion problem, showing that our algorithm exhibits the fastest initial error reduction compared with other methods from current literature.
item.dc:creator: Ruochen Wu, Xu Du, Mohammadreza Doostmohammadian, Karl H. Johansson, Apostolos I. Rikos

item.title: WSINDy for Model Predictive Control with Applications to Fusion, Drones, and Chaos
item.description: arXiv:2604.23269v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The control of complex dynamical systems remains a fundamental challenge in science and engineering, where strong nonlinearities, the presence of noise, and computational constraints often pose significant obstacles in traditional control approaches. Recent advances in data-driven methods, particularly system identification techniques, have shown a powerful alternative by providing fast, parsimonious, interpretable models that are well-suited for model predictive control (MPC). Building on these developments, the present article embeds WSINDy with actuation inputs (WSINDYc) within a MPC framework. Compared to benchmark data-driven methods, WSINDYc enables a more robust identification of the governing dynamics, particularly in the presence of high noise levels, resulting in more accurate and efficient control. The capabilities of the proposed WSINDY-MPC framework are demonstrated on a range of problems, including a tokamak plasma boundary model that includes main ion gas puff actuation, drone tracking and collision avoidance, the chaotic Lorenz system, and a simplified flight control model for an F-8 aircraft. The proposed framework achieves superior performance in the presence of noise, enabling longer prediction horizons, lower trajectory tracking error, and a more reliable obstacle clearance, while simultaneously achieving lower MPC cost values compared to the baseline methods.
item.dc:creator: Cristian L\'opez, Mckenna Partridge, Sebastian De Pascuale, Jeremy Lore, Andrew Christlieb, Stephen Becker, David M. Bortz

item.title: PREFER: Personalized Review Summarization with Online Preference Learning
item.description: arXiv:2605.05911v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Product reviews significantly influence purchasing decisions on e-commerce platforms. However, the sheer volume of reviews can overwhelm users, obscuring information most relevant to their individual needs. Existing e-commerce summarization systems typically produce generic, static summaries that fail to account for the fact that (i) different users prioritize different product characteristics, and (ii) these preferences may evolve with interactions. To address these challenges, we propose an online learning framework that generates personalized summaries for each user by representing user interests in a latent aspect space and selecting preference-aligned review evidence. Our system then iteratively refines its understanding of user preferences by incorporating feedback on the generated summaries directly over time. We evaluate our framework on Amazon Reviews'23 using controlled feedback simulations and robustness checks with held-out-history, independent-embedding, and external LLM-based evaluators. These experiments show improvements in preference-aligned evidence selection under the evaluated feedback settings. A separate human-based study finds that scenario-conditioned summaries are preferred over generic (uniformly-aggregated) alternatives in 69.9% of paired comparisons.
item.dc:creator: Millend Roy, Agostino Capponi, Vineet Goyal

item.title: Generalized Wasserstein Flow Matching: Nested Couplings for Point Cloud Generation
item.description: arXiv:2605.08424v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We formulate flow matching on probability measures over probability measures. Directly from the Wasserstein-on-Wasserstein (WoW) continuity equation, we show that admissible nested outer and inner couplings induce a valid metameasure flow and non-local velocity field. Validity requires neither optimal plans nor a smooth manifold. Practically, this opens up the design space of multisample flow matching: exact Wasserstein plans are distinguished by energy and straightness, while sliced and lazy linear plans yield scalable alternatives. Point-cloud experiments, including controlled Bures-Wasserstein and Euclidean minibatch baselines, demonstrate the resulting geometry-cost trade-off.
item.dc:creator: Moritz Piening, Richard Duong, Gabriele Steidl

item.title: Projected McKean--Vlasov Dynamics for Entropic Weak Optimal Transport
item.description: arXiv:2605.30560v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Unlike classical optimal transport, weak transport costs depend nonlinearly on the conditional law of couplings. This feature is essential in problems involving barycenter, conditional moments, and martingale-type constraints. Meanwhile, such conditional dependence makes ordinary Wasserstein geometry insufficient and calls instead for an adapted Wasserstein viewpoint. In this paper, we investigate the entropy-regularized weak optimal transport via gradient flows in adapted Wasserstein space. We derive, from the formal tangent structure of adapted Wasserstein space and the projection onto the set of couplings with prescribed marginals, a coupled McKean--Vlasov SDE. A novel and subtle term is a projection that, at each $Y$-location, averages a weak-transport force that already depends on the conditional law of $Y$ given $X$, thereby preserving marginals while retaining the nonlinear weak-transport structure. Under mild integrability and regularity assumptions, we prove weak existence and uniqueness in law for this projected McKean--Vlasov equation. We then prove that the flow converges, in the adapted Wasserstein topology, to the unique minimizer of the entropic weak optimal transport problem. We also describe a particle approximation and illustrate the dynamics on optimal transport and martingale optimal transport examples.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Sauldubois, Xin Zhang

item.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for coupled stiff transport systems
item.description: arXiv:2606.21236v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN) struggle with stiff, regime-changing transport equations due to instability, loss imbalance, and violations of physical consistency. This paper investigates these failures through the Marshak wave equations, a canonical benchmark from radiative transport, where initial and boundary conditions differ by up to 12 orders of magnitude, and proposes modifications to the standard PINN framework to overcome them. Three modifications are introduced: a ScaledSigmoid final activation enforcing physical bounds and positivity of the unknowns; a logarithmic MSE loss replacing the standard quadratic loss for initial and boundary conditions, enabling training across extreme scale disparities; and explicit enforcement of global conservation laws as an additional physics loss term. Monte Carlo sampling with exponential time weighting is used throughout. The proposed framework recovers the Marshak wave dynamics - including the hot, cold, and wave-front regions - in good agreement with a reference Implicit Monte Carlo solution (sub-millimeter absolute error on the front position, although the relative error remains substantial at early times), with run times under 5 minutes. Ablation studies confirm that each ingredient is essential: linear activation, absence of the logarithmic loss, or removal of the PDE term each independently cause the method to fail qualitatively. This work identifies and resolves three concrete failure modes of standard PINN on stiff hyperbolic systems with nonlinear coupling. The combination of bounded activations, scale-aware loss functions, and conservation law enforcement constitutes a framework validated on the present one-dimensional Marshak wave problem, with potential extension to other coupled stiff transport systems in engineering.
item.dc:creator: Laetitia Laguzet, Gabriel Turinici

item.title: SLAB: Time-Lag-Aware Deep Reinforcement Learning for Flexible Job-Shop Scheduling in PPVC Module Factories
item.description: arXiv:2607.11725v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Prefabricated prefinished volumetric construction (PPVC) builds room-sized modules in factories that operate as flexible job shops. A module waits 12 to 48 h after casting, waterproofing, and painting, while its station is free for other modules. Existing learned dispatchers release the next operation before this wait ends, so their plans need repair. This paper presents SLAB (Scheduling under time-Lags with an Admissible Bound), a decision process for dispatchers trained by deep reinforcement learning. Its transition releases a module only after its wait, and its reward is the decrease of a proven lower bound that includes the waits. Training on 10-module orders with halved waits also teaches the policy the station contention of larger orders. On three existing networks, repaired plans are 42% to 133% longer than the same network's schedules inside SLAB. On orders generated from Singapore's PPVC guidebook, one trained policy gives schedules 2.2% to 8.1% shorter than the shortest-processing-time rule at 10 to 80 modules. At 50 and 80 modules, it outperforms a time-lag memetic algorithm by 6.7% and 7.4% and constraint-programming search started from that rule's schedule and given 600 s by 6.6% and 7.6%. The memetic algorithm gives shorter schedules on orders of 10 modules, and the same search given 300 s on orders of 10 and 20 modules. A module factory can therefore train one dispatcher on small orders and run it without a solver on production batches of 50 to 80 modules.
item.dc:creator: Ziheng Zhang, Dhivya Dharshini Kannan, Wei Zhang

item.title: Regularity-Aware Stochastic MGDA with Adaptive Per-Iterate Conflict-Avoidant Update
item.description: arXiv:2607.15412v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Multi-objective learning (MOL) aims to optimize multiple objectives simultaneously. The multi-gradient descent algorithm (MGDA) constructs a common descent or conflict-avoidant (CA) direction by solving a gradient-aggregation subproblem. In stochastic settings, the vanilla stochastic MGDA method, SMG, replaces full-batch gradients with mini-batch estimates, causing bias in the resulting CA direction. Existing analyses control this error using continuity of the CA-direction mapping, but do not distinguish how its sensitivity varies with the geometry of the MGDA subproblem. Motivated by this limitation, we show that the MGDA direction map is Lipschitz continuous under reduced nondegeneracy, whereas its general \(1/2\)-H\"older exponent on bounded sets is sharp. This geometry motivates the Multi-objective Regularity-aware (MoRe) method, which retains adaptive MGDA aggregation in the regular regime and switches to a fixed-weight linear scalarization (LS) near degeneracy. The fallback branch skips the MGDA subproblem solve, which can reduce aggregation cost on fallback iterations while avoiding a potentially noise-sensitive update. Theoretically, we establish a per-iterate CA guarantee, and a \(\widetilde{\mathcal O}(T^{-1})\) convergence rate, improving upon the previously established \(\widetilde{\mathcal O}(T^{-1/4})\) SMG guarantee, where \(\widetilde{\mathcal O}\) hides logarithmic factors. Experiments demonstrate favorable multi-task performance and convergence behavior consistent with the theoretical rate.
item.dc:creator: Chentong Huang, Lisha Chen

item.title: The Tamed Subgradient Unadjusted Langevin Algorithm beyond Convexity
item.description: arXiv:2608.06283v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the problem of sampling from target distributions whose potentials are simultaneously non-smooth, subject to superlinear gradient growth, and non-convex. We introduce the Subgradient Tamed Unadjusted Langevin Algorithm (SG-TULA), a discretisation of the Langevin diffusion that operates directly on subgradients, without relying on computationally demanding smoothing procedures. To handle the superlinear regime, taming techniques are employed to produce a stable, explicit scheme. We derive non-asymptotic convergence bounds in Wasserstein-2 distance, with all constants tracked explicitly in terms of dimension and inverse temperature, improving upon the currently known rates for subgradient-based Langevin algorithms. We further provide excess risk estimates for the associated optimisation problem. We verify the assumptions, with explicit constants, for the regularized pretraining potential of a LLM in the GPT-2 lineage and the boosted coordinate-wise variant of SG-TULA pretrains the former competitively against finetuned AdamW and Muon, for which no comparable non-asymptotic guarantees are presently available.
item.dc:creator: Iosif Lytras, Nikolaos Makras, Sotirios Sabanis

item.title: Online Multi-Level Aggregation with Maximum Delay
item.description: arXiv:2608.06796v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study Multi-Level Aggregation with Maximum Delay (MLA-MD) on finite weighted rooted trees. Each service pays for a rooted subtree and for the maximum waiting time among the requests it clears. For the offline problem, we give an exact polynomial-time algorithm that computes both the optimum and an optimal service schedule. For the online problem, we give a deterministic $2$-competitive algorithm and, against an oblivious adversary, a randomized $e/(e-1)$-competitive algorithm. Both competitive ratios are optimal, even on rooted paths. We also extend the offline result and both online guarantees to service systems with submodular costs.
item.dc:creator: Tianhang Lu, Runtian Ren, Shengcai Liu, Ke Tang

item.title: Matrix nearness problems: Do real inputs admit real solutions?
item.description: arXiv:2609.14828v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a real square matrix $A$ and a nonempty closed target set of complex matrices $\mathcal{E}$, invariant by complex conjugation and containing real matrices, does the subset of $\mathcal{E}$ consisting of the matrices nearest to $A$ in the Frobenius distance always contain a real matrix? We give negative answers when $\mathcal{E}$ is either the set of normal matrices (solving a question posed by N. Higham) or the set of matrices whose eigenvalues lie in the closed left half-plane (solving a question posed by the first author and F. Poloni). For the latter problem, we also argue that the ratio between the real and complex distances is unbounded in every dimension $n\geq 3$, and this holds for every distance induced by a unitarily invariant norm. For both problems and $n \geq 3$, we show that a real input $A$ uniformly drawn from the unit sphere $\|A\|_F=1$ has no real minimizer over $\mathcal{E}$ with probability strictly between $0$ and $1$. Beyond these two cases, we prove for an arbitrary nonempty closed target sets $\mathcal{E}$ that, for almost every real input, either $\mathcal{E}$ contains a unique nearest matrix which is real, or every nearest matrix in $\mathcal{E}$ is nonreal.
item.dc:creator: Vanni Noferini, Matvei Zhukov

item.title: Strong laws, random monotone vector fields and gradient flows on metric spaces of nonpositive curvature
item.description: arXiv:2609.16439v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish a probabilistic Lie-Trotter-Kato formula for the gradient flow generated by an integral function over suitable separable Hadamard spaces. This result leverages Stojkovi\'c's Lie-Trotter-Kato formula for gradient flows of sums of convex functions and Ba\v{c}\'ak's result relating resolvent and gradient flow convergence, along with a strong law of large numbers for normal convex integrands. For separable Hilbert spaces and locally compact Hadamard spaces, these strong laws follow from results of King and Wets and Artstein and Wets, respectively, but we crucially go beyond these examples by establishing a new such strong law for normal convex integrands on all Hadamard spaces whose tangent cones are isometric to Hilbert spaces, a class that includes non-Hilbertian, non-locally compact examples such as infinite-dimensional hyperbolic space. This new strong law arises as a combination of a strong law of large numbers for integrable random monotone vector fields on Hilbert-Hadamard spaces, that is, Hadamard spaces whose tangent cones all embed isometrically into Hilbert spaces, extending a result of Salim from Hilbert spaces, together with a new result on the interchangeability of the subdifferential and the integral, which we establish for $L^2$-Lipschitz integrands. This latter ingredient provides, to our knowledge, the first nonlinear version of (a particular case of) a previous result due variously to Ioffe and Tikhomirov, Levin, Hiriart-Urruty, Thibault as well as Rockafellar and Wets. On the way to this strong law for random monotone vector fields, we also establish a distribution-uniform generalization of Sturm's strong law of large numbers for inductive means of $L^1$-sequences of i.i.d. random variables on Hadamard spaces via a new effective non-asymptotic concentration inequality. Throughout the paper, we highlight various remaining open problems.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Pischke

item.title: The Critical Line Algorithm and the Constrained LASSO: One Curve, Two Literatures
item.description: arXiv:2609.25704v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Many statistical procedures compute an entire solution path rather than a single estimator. For one class the path is piecewise linear, traced corner to corner by an active-set homotopy. Two of its members coincide exactly: under $\Sigma=X^\top X$ and $\mu=X^\top y$ the gross-exposure-constrained mean--variance program and the constrained LASSO trace the same piecewise-linear curve, and they keep doing so under arbitrary linear equality and inequality constraints. Which parameter is swept, a leverage budget or a return tilt, is not a choice the curve notices: under a homogeneous mandate the two sweeps differ by a scalar. A mandate that holds the portfolio invested costs a radial rescaling instead, and the efficient frontier is that curve rescaled; its corners pass unnoticed because the frontier is continuously differentiable where they fall. We give the map between the two parametrisations and the single way it degenerates. That mean--variance selection and the LASSO instantiate one parametric quadratic program is prior art (G\"artner, Jaggi and Maria, 2012). The Critical Line Algorithm itself lies off that route, and the correspondence established here is new. The identity is one of curves, not of statistical experiments. The map between the parametrisations is computed from the data, so the geometry of the path transfers while quantities averaged over the response do not. We cross that boundary deliberately and give the degrees of freedom of the constrained fit under arbitrary linear constraints. In the long-only, fully invested case it is the expected number of holdings away from a bound, less one.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Schmelzer, Trevor Hastie

item.title: Geometry-Dependent Approximation for Non-Monotone $k$-Submodular Maximization
item.description: arXiv:2610.04049v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the maximization of a nonnegative $k$-submodular function, not assumed monotone, in which each of $n$ elements receives one of $k\ge2$ labels or stays unselected and the selected elements must satisfy a constraint. For a compact convex down-closed region $P\subseteq[0,1]^n$ of fractional selection vectors, the diagonal level $\zeta(P)=\max\{t\in[0,1]:t(1,\ldots,1)\in P\}$ is the largest selection probability that can be given to all elements at once; it equals $r/n$ for a uniform matroid of rank $r$, and $\zeta(P)=1$ means that the constraint is vacuous. We give approximation coefficients that increase continuously with $\zeta$. They come from one inequality for the multilinear extension of the objective: the algorithm computes an action without querying the objective, and objective feedback gives a comparator-independent update direction. For $k\ge3$, feasibility of the action reduces to three polynomial inequalities in one variable; for $k=2$ the profile is closed form. At $\zeta=0$ the coefficients are $0.4456\ldots$ for $k=2$ and $0.4541\ldots$ for every $k\ge3$. For every finite $k\ge3$ they reach $1/2$ above an explicit level, which is $0.4026\ldots$ for $k=3,4,5$, and at $\zeta=1$ they reach $1/2$ for $k=2$, $(\sqrt{17}-3)/2$ for $k=3,4$, and $k/(2k-1)$ for $k\ge5$. Online linear optimization gives $O(\sqrt T)$ approximate regret, with gradient feedback or with value queries made after each action. The coefficients carry over to matroids, with expected and high-probability guarantees, and to any fixed number of knapsacks: the zero-level coefficients hold on every instance, and the larger ones when items are small or when prefix enumeration keeps the diagonal level on one branch. For one budget the enumeration exponent is $O(1/\varepsilon)$.

item.title: Symmetry-breaking in a discrete-choice LQG mean field game
item.description: arXiv:2610.05730v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Mean-field games provide a continuum framework for modeling the dynamics of large, interacting populations of non-cooperative agents. This paper studies symmetry-breaking in a finite-horizon, two-choice min-LQG mean-field game in which identical agents with linear stochastic dynamics choose one of two equally desirable terminal destinations, while trading off control effort against social pressure to conform. The model has an odd symmetry between the two destinations and therefore always admits a symmetric, dynamic Nash equilibrium in which the population splits evenly between them, producing a deadlock collective state at final time. Numerical studies have suggested that, as the penalty for social nonconformity increases, this symmetric equilibrium loses stability as a fixed point of an associated scalar, self-consistency map, and asymmetric consensus Nash equilibria emerge, where most agents select the same destination. By analyzing the linearized forward-backward PDE system through the scalar map representation, we provide a proof of this loss of stability of the symmetric equilibrium. Together with the odd symmetry of the map, this implies the existence of symmetry-broken mean-field game equilibria corresponding to consensus on either destination.

item.title: When Momentum Helps Polyak--Ruppert Averaging
item.description: arXiv:2610.27990v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Polyak--Ruppert averaging gives SGD and momentum methods the same asymptotic covariance. We characterize how fast finite runs reach it and how far they can be parallelized. For strongly convex quadratics with additive noise, we prove an online--offline bridge: the empirical risk minimizer on the samples of a tail average is one Newton step from the tail-averaged query point of any online procedure. For SGD, heavy ball, and Nesterov's method with constant momentum, this step is a boundary term at the two ends of the tail and splits the gap to the offline estimator into center, covariance, and shape errors. Necessary and sufficient conditions show that, on the least curved direction, the center error sets the pace: SGD needs $m\gg\kappa^2$ rounds but momentum only $m\gg\kappa$, where $\kappa$ is the condition number, so at sample size $N$ the critical batch size grows from $\Theta(\sqrt{N}/\kappa)$ to $\Theta(\sqrt{N/\kappa})$. The covariance error separates the momentum methods: heavy ball has relative variance excess $\Theta(\kappa^{3/2}/m)$ along the stiffest direction, whereas Nesterov has relative error $O(\sqrt{\kappa}/m)$ in every direction. The shape error is method-independent by a Berry--Esseen bound uniform in $\kappa$ and batch size, so confidence intervals are valid when the other two errors vanish. We further examine how the conclusions change under heavy-tailed or state-dependent noise and clipping, and establish a first-order comparison with ERM for nonlinear Nesterov averaging under explicit conditions.

item.title: Deflation-Based Spectral Preconditioning for the Conjugate Gradient Method on Perturbed Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.28808v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider sequences of large symmetric positive-definite linear systems in which spectral information from a reference matrix $A$ is reused to accelerate the solution of a nearby system with perturbed matrix $A(t)=A+tE$, where $E$ is symmetric, $\|E\|_F=1$, and $t\geq0$ is the perturbation size. We compare deflated conjugate gradient (deflated CG) with preconditioned CG (PCG) equipped with a scaled spectral preconditioner constructed from the same spectral information of $A$. First, we derive an energy-norm error characterization of deflated CG. We then use perturbation analysis to show that, after one additional PCG iteration, the squared PCG error is bounded, up to terms of order $t^2$, by an explicit multiple of the squared deflated CG error. This result clarifies the role of the scaling parameter in the preconditioner. Experiments show that the scaled spectral preconditioner recovers much of the convergence improvement provided by deflation while requiring fewer products with $A(t)$.
